mainTopic: The end of the book of אדם הראשון list, the death of רבה בר נחמני, the story of רבי שמעון בן חלפתא, and the return to the משנה on feeding workers by local custom
overview: This amud first finishes a list from the book of אדם הראשון. שמואל ירחינאה will heal רבי. רבי and רבי נתן are the end of the משנה, and רב אשי and רבינא are the end of הוראה, with a פסוק given as a memory aid. Then the גמרא tells the long story of רבה בר נחמני's death. He was slandered to the king and ran from the king's messenger, and miracles saved him. While he hid and learned in a swamp, the heavenly yeshiva needed him to decide a doubt about צרעת. He died saying 'טהור, טהור', and heaven, the חכמים and even nature honored him. A short story about רבי שמעון בן חלפתא and a cooling wind follows. Then the גמרא goes back to the משנה about feeding workers. The word הכל teaches that an employer cannot change the local eating custom. The story of רבן יוחנן בן מתיא seems to contradict the rule, so the גמרא says words are missing from the משנה. It begins the missing line, 'if he promised them food', which continues on the next amud.

steps.title: שמואל ירחינאה will be called a wise doctor and will heal רבי
steps.stepSummary: The book of אדם הראשון says that שמואל ירחינאה will be called 'חכים' but not 'רבי', and that רבי's healing will come through him.
steps.simpleTranslation: He will be called 'wise one,' but he will not be called 'רבי.' And רבי's healing will come through him.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is finishing a quote from the book of אדם הראשון about שמואל ירחינאה, who was רבי's doctor. It says what title he will have and what he will do.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Even though שמואל was a great חכם, he would never be given סמיכה, so he would not get the title 'רבי'. He would still have a special job: he would be the one to cure רבי.

keyTerms.meaning: Wise one; here it is the title for a doctor or scholar

phrases.english: He will be called 'wise one,'
but he will not be called 'Rabbi.'
And Rabbi's healing will be through him.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the quote from the book of אדם הראשון that began before this section.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: שמואל ירחינאה is called 'חכים', not 'רבי', and he will be the one to heal רבי.

steps.title: The end of the משנה and the end of הוראה
steps.stepSummary: רבי and רבי נתן are the last of the משנה period. רב אשי and רבינא are the last of the הוראה (אמוראים) period.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי and רבי נתן are the end of the משנה. רב אשי and רבינא are the end of instruction.
steps.whatsHappening: Another line from the same book: it names who closes each big period of Torah teaching.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'סוף משנה' means the last of the תנאים, the ones who finished the משנה. 'סוף הוראה' means the last of the אמוראים, the ones who finished the גמרא. These are two separate eras, and each one has a closing pair.

keyTerms.meaning: The end of the משנה period (the last תנאים)
The end of the period of teaching and ruling (the last אמוראים)
The אמוראים who finished putting together the גמרא

steps.whyThisMatters: This is a classic source for the idea that רב אשי and רבינא closed the תלמוד בבלי.

phrases.english: Rabbi and Rabbi Natan are the end of the Mishna.
Rav Ashi and Ravina are the end of instruction.
phrases.notes: 'Instruction' here means the era of the אמוראים, whose teachings make up the גמרא.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds the next line from the same book of אדם הראשון.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי and רבי נתן close the משנה period, and רב אשי and רבינא close the הוראה period.

steps.title: A פסוק to help remember רב אשי and רבינא
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא gives a memory aid from תהלים: 'מקדשי' hints to רב אשי, 'אבינה' hints to רבינא, and 'לאחריתם' hints to the end.
steps.simpleTranslation: And your memory aid is: 'Until I came into the sanctuary of God and understood their end.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a פסוק as a 'סימן' (memory aid) so we remember that רב אשי and רבינא are the end of הוראה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is not a proof. It is a hint to help us remember. The word 'אבינה' sounds like רבינא, the word 'מקדשי' points to רב אשי, and 'לאחריתם' (their end) points to the closing of הוראה.

keyTerms.meaning: I will understand; it hints to רבינא

steps.confusionAlert: A סימן is only a memory trick. It is not a source that proves the fact.
steps.whatToRemember: The book of אדם הראשון ends here: שמואל ירחינאה heals רבי, and the last names of the משנה and of הוראה are given, with a פסוק to help remember them.

phrases.english: And your memory aid is:
"Until I came into the sanctuary of God,
and understood their end."
phrases.notes: 'אבינה' sounds like רבינא, and 'their end' points to the end of הוראה.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a memory aid for the fact taught in step 2.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The פסוק 'עד אבוא אל מקדשי אל אבינה לאחריתם' serves as a memory aid for רב אשי and רבינא as סוף הוראה.

steps.title: רבה בר נחמני died because of persecution
steps.stepSummary: רב כהנא reports from רב חמא that רבה בר נחמני died because of a שמד (a decree of persecution).
steps.simpleTranslation: רב כהנא said: רב חמא, the son of חסא's daughter, told me that רבה בר נחמני died because of persecution.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts a new story about the greatness of the חכמים. It begins with the headline: רבה בר נחמני died because of a time of persecution.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The story is passed along through a chain: רב חמא told רב כהנא. Opening with the ending, his death, prepares us for the details of how it happened.

keyTerms.meaning: Because of a decree of persecution
He passed away (literally, his soul rested)

phrases.english: Rav Kahana said:
Rav Chama told me,
the son of the daughter of Chasa:
Rabba bar Nachmani
died because of persecution.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב כָּהֲנָא, אִישְׁתַּעִי לִי רַב חָמָא בַּר בְּרַתֵּיה דְּחַסָּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new story, separate from the book of אדם הראשון.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבה בר נחמני died because of a time of persecution.

steps.title: רבה is slandered to the king
steps.stepSummary: People slandered רבה at the king's palace. They said he kept twelve thousand Jews from paying the king's head tax for two months every year.
steps.simpleTranslation: They slandered him in the king's palace. They said: There is one man among the Jews who keeps twelve thousand Jewish men away from the king's head tax, one month in summer and one month in winter.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains how the trouble started: someone informed on רבה to the government.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The charge was that thousands of people gathered by רבה to learn for a month in summer and a month in winter. Because of this, the king lost out on the head tax. The king saw this as a threat to his money, and that is why he went after רבה.

keyTerms.meaning: A month in summer and a month in winter

phrases.english: They slandered him in the king's palace;
they said: There is one man among the Jews

phrases.aramaic: דְּקָא מְבַטֵּל תְּרֵיסַר אַלְפֵי גַּבְרֵי מִיִּשְׂרָאֵל
phrases.english: who keeps twelve thousand men of Israel away
for a month in summer and a month in winter
from the king's head tax.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the reason behind the persecution mentioned in step 4.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The accusation was that רבה caused twelve thousand Jews to miss the king's head tax for two months a year.

steps.title: The king's messenger chases רבה as he runs from town to town
steps.stepSummary: The king sent a messenger after רבה but could not find him. רבה ran through many places and ended up back in פומבדיתא.
steps.simpleTranslation: They sent the king's messenger after him, but he did not find him. He fled from פומבדיתא to אקרא, from אקרא to אגמא, from אגמא to שחין, from שחין to צריפא, from צריפא to עינא דמים, and from עינא דמים back to פומבדיתא.
steps.whatsHappening: The government tries to arrest רבה. He escapes by moving from place to place.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The long list of towns shows how hard רבה ran and how long he was chased. His route makes a full circle back to פומבדיתא, which sets up where he will be found next.

keyTerms.meaning: פומבדיתא, the town where רבה led the yeshiva

phrases.english: They sent the king's messenger after him,
but he did not find him.
He fled and went from Pumbedita to Akra,
from Akra to Agma, and from Agma to Shichin,
and from Shichin to Tzerifa, and from Tzerifa to Eina Demayim,
and from Eina Demayim to Pumbedita.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Shows what the king did after hearing the accusation, and how רבה escaped.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבה escaped the king's messenger by fleeing through many towns and coming back to פומבדיתא.

steps.title: The messenger finds רבה's inn, and his face is turned backward
steps.stepSummary: The messenger came by chance to the inn where רבה was. After he was served, his face was miraculously turned backward.
steps.simpleTranslation: He was found in פומבדיתא. The king's messenger happened to come to the same inn where רבה was. They brought a tray before him and gave him two cups to drink. When they took the tray away from him, his face was turned backward.
steps.whatsHappening: The chase ends in פומבדיתא, where the messenger happens to arrive at רבה's inn. Then something strange happens to the messenger, and this sets up the next part of the story.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The messenger ends up at רבה's hiding place by 'chance,' so רבה is in danger. Heaven steps in: the messenger's face is turned backward, which stops him from acting. The next step tells what the people at the inn do about it.

keyTerms.meaning: A tray or small table for food

phrases.english: In Pumbedita he was found.
The king's messenger happened to arrive
at that inn where Rabba was.
They brought a tray before him
and gave him two cups to drink,
and when they lifted the tray away from before him,
his face turned around to the back.
phrases.notes: This is a miracle: the messenger's own face got twisted backward.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the chase from step 6 to the meeting at the inn and the miracle.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: When the king's messenger reached רבה's inn, his face was miraculously turned backward.

steps.title: The attendants ask what to do with the injured messenger
steps.stepSummary: The people at the inn ask רבה what to do, because the injured man works for the king.
steps.simpleTranslation: They said to רבה: What should we do for him? He is the king's man!
steps.whatsHappening: The people at the inn are afraid because the king's messenger is hurt, and they ask רבה for help. This question sets up רבה's answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Leaving the king's officer with his face turned backward could bring serious trouble on everyone. So they turn to רבה, who seems to know how to fix it.

keyTerms.meaning: the king's man, a royal officer

phrases.english: They said to him: What should we do for him?
phrases.notes: The first 'him' is רבה; the second is the injured messenger.

phrases.english: He is the king's man!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Reacts to the miracle in Step 7, where the messenger's face was turned backward.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: How to heal the king's messenger.

steps.title: רבה tells them how to heal the messenger
steps.stepSummary: רבה gives instructions: serve him, give him one cup, take the tray away. They do it and he is healed.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to them: Bring a tray before him, give him one cup to drink, then take the tray away and he will be healed. They did this and he was healed.
steps.whatsHappening: רבה answers the question by telling them exactly how to heal the messenger. They follow the instructions, and it works.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In Step 7 the injury came right after he was served. Now the steps of the meal are done again and the tray is taken away, and the injury goes away with it.

keyTerms.meaning: a tray or small table for food

phrases.english: He said to them: Bring a tray before him,
and give him one cup to drink,
and lift the tray away from before him, and he will be healed.
They did this to him, and he was healed.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the attendants' question from Step 8.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Serve him, give him one cup, remove the tray, and he will be healed.

steps.title: The messenger finds רבה and promises not to reveal him
steps.stepSummary: The messenger realizes רבה must be there, finds him, and promises to keep his location secret even if killed, but not if beaten.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said: I know for sure that the man I am looking for is here. He searched for him and found him. He said: I will leave here. If they kill me, I will not reveal where he is. But if they beat me, I will reveal it.
steps.whatsHappening: The messenger understands that this miracle points to רבה, so he searches and finds him. He then makes a deal to protect רבה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The miracle and its cure showed the messenger that a holy man was there. His promise has a limit: he can face death without telling, but he admits he could not hold out under beating.

phrases.english: He said: I know for sure
that the man I am looking for is here.
He searched for him and found him.
He said: I will go away from here.

phrases.aramaic: אִי מִקְטָל קָטְלוּ לְהָהוּא גַּבְרָא – לָא מְגַלֵּינָא,
phrases.english: If they kill that man, I will not reveal,
phrases.notes: 'That man' is a polite way of saying 'me'. He doesn't want to say 'kill me' outright.

phrases.english: but if they beat him, I will reveal.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר: מִידָּע יָדַעְנָא דְּגַבְרָא דְּקָא בָעֵינָא הָכָא הוּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After being healed, the messenger draws a conclusion from the miracle.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The messenger finds רבה and promises secrecy unless he is tortured.

steps.title: רבה is locked up, escapes, and learns in a swamp
steps.stepSummary: רבה is brought to the messenger and locked in a room. He prays, the wall breaks, and he flees to a swamp, where he sits and learns.
steps.simpleTranslation: They brought רבה before him. He put him into a room and slammed the door in his face. רבה prayed, the wall broke apart, and he fled to a swamp. He sat on a palm-tree stump and learned.
steps.whatsHappening: רבה is caught and locked up, but a miracle sets him free. He hides in a swamp and keeps learning תורה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This step moves רבה to the swamp where the rest of the story takes place. His constant learning there becomes important in Step 14.

phrases.english: They brought him before him.
He brought him into a room
and slammed the door in his face.
He prayed for mercy, and the wall broke apart.
He fled and went to a swamp.

phrases.aramaic: הֲוָה יָתֵיב אַגִּירְדָּא דְּדִקּוּלָא וְקָא גָרֵיס.
phrases.english: He was sitting on the stump of a palm tree and learning.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues from the messenger's promise. רבה is brought to him.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבה escapes miraculously and learns alone in a swamp.

steps.title: The heavenly yeshiva discusses בהרת and white hair
steps.stepSummary: The scene moves to the heavenly yeshiva. The basic rule is stated: if the בהרת came first, the person is טמא. If the white hair came first, he is טהור.
steps.simpleTranslation: They were discussing in the heavenly yeshiva: If the בהרת came before the white hair, he is impure. If the white hair came before the בהרת, he is pure.
steps.whatsHappening: The story jumps to heaven, where a discussion about נגעים is happening. This step gives the basic rule and sets up the real argument in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Everyone agrees on these two clear cases. The rule depends on which sign of צרעת appeared first. That is why a case where we don't know the order becomes a problem.

keyTerms.meaning: a bright white spot on the skin, a sign of צרעת
white hair inside the spot, a sign of impurity

steps.confusionAlert: The two cases in this step are not the argument. Both sides agree on them. The argument is only about the case of doubt in the next step.

phrases.english: They were arguing in the heavenly yeshiva:

phrases.aramaic: אִם בַּהֶרֶת קוֹדֶמֶת לְשֵׂעָר לָבָן – טָמֵא,
phrases.english: If the bright spot came before the white hair, he is impure;

phrases.aramaic: וְאִם שֵׂעָר לָבָן קוֹדֵם לַבַּהֶרֶת – טָהוֹר.
phrases.english: and if the white hair came before the bright spot, he is pure.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: While רבה is learning on earth, the story shifts to a discussion in heaven.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A בהרת before white hair is טמא. White hair before a בהרת is טהור.

steps.title: A doubt in heaven, and רבה בר נחמני is chosen to decide
steps.stepSummary: In a case where we don't know which came first, הקב"ה says טהור and the whole heavenly yeshiva says טמא. They choose רבה בר נחמני to decide, because he called himself unique in נגעים and אהלות.
steps.simpleTranslation: In a case of doubt, the Holy One says pure, and the whole heavenly yeshiva says impure. They said: Who will decide? רבה בר נחמני will decide, because רבה בר נחמני said: I am unique in נגעים, I am unique in אהלות.
steps.whatsHappening: This is the real argument: what to do when the order of the signs is unknown. Heaven wants רבה בר נחמני to settle it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The rule from Step 12 does not cover a case of doubt, so there are two opinions. רבה is picked because of his own claim to be the expert in these laws. This explains why heaven wants to bring him up.

keyTerms.meaning: will decide, will settle the argument
laws of impurity spread by a dead body under a roof

steps.whyThisMatters: This explains the story's reason for רבה's death: heaven needed his expertise to settle a question of תורה.

phrases.aramaic: סָפֵק – הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא אוֹמֵר: טָהוֹר,
phrases.english: In a case of doubt, the Holy One, Blessed be He, says: pure,
phrases.notes: The doubt is whether the spot or the white hair came first.

phrases.english: and the whole heavenly yeshiva says: impure.
And they said: Who will decide?
רבה בר נחמני will decide.
For רבה בר נחמני said:

phrases.aramaic: אֲנִי יָחִיד בִּנְגָעִים, אֲנִי יָחִיד בְּאֹהָלוֹת.
phrases.english: I am unique in נגעים; I am unique in אהלות.

steps.triggerLanguage: סָפֵק – הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא אוֹמֵר: טָהוֹר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the agreed cases to the case of doubt, which is what they argue about.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: In a case of doubt, הקב"ה says טהור and the heavenly yeshiva says טמא. רבה בר נחמני is chosen to decide.

steps.title: The מלאך המוות cannot reach רבה while he learns
steps.stepSummary: Heaven sends a messenger for רבה, but the מלאך המוות cannot come near him because he never stops learning.
steps.simpleTranslation: They sent a messenger after him. The מלאך המוות could not come near him, because his mouth never stopped learning.
steps.whatsHappening: Heaven tries to take רבה up, but his nonstop learning protects him.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This connects the swamp scene from Step 11 to the heavenly argument. Constant תורה learning holds back the מלאך המוות, so something has to interrupt it.

phrases.english: They sent a messenger after him.
phrases.notes: This is a messenger from heaven now, not the king's messenger from before.

phrases.aramaic: לָא הֲוָה מָצֵי מַלְאַךְ הַמָּוֶת לְמִקְרַב לֵיהּ,
phrases.english: The Angel of Death could not come near him,

phrases.aramaic: מִדְּלָא הֲוָה קָא פָסֵיק פּוּמֵּיהּ מִגִּרְסֵיהּ.
phrases.english: because his mouth did not stop from his learning.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Acts on the heavenly decision from Step 13 to bring רבה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The מלאך המוות cannot take רבה while he keeps learning.

steps.title: A noise in the reeds, and רבה asks to die
steps.stepSummary: A wind rustles the reeds. רבה thinks soldiers are coming and says he would rather die than be handed over to the government.
steps.simpleTranslation: Meanwhile a wind blew and rustled among the reeds. He thought it was a troop of horsemen. He said: Let me die, and not be handed over to the government.
steps.whatsHappening: A simple wind makes רבה think the king's soldiers have found him. He says he prefers death to being captured.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is the moment his learning is interrupted, since he stops to speak. He also asks for death himself, which explains how the story reaches its end.

phrases.english: Meanwhile, a wind blew
and rustled among the reeds.
He thought it was a troop of horsemen.
He said: Let that man's soul be at rest,
phrases.notes: Like the messenger before, 'that man' means himself. He is asking to die.

phrases.english: and not be handed over to the government.

steps.triggerLanguage: אַדְּהָכִי נְשַׁב זִיקָא וַאֲוַושׁ בֵּינֵי קְנֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Shows what interrupts the nonstop learning described in Step 14.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Thinking soldiers had come, רבה asks to die rather than be captured.

steps.title: רבה dies saying 'pure, pure'
steps.stepSummary: As רבה בר נחמני dies, he says 'טהור, טהור', and a בת קול praises him because his soul left with the word טהור.
steps.simpleTranslation: As he was dying, he said: 'Pure, pure.' A heavenly voice came out and said: 'Fortunate are you, רבה בר נחמני, that your body is pure and your soul left with the word pure.'
steps.whatsHappening: רבה gives his ruling on the heavenly question with his last words, and heaven praises him for it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The heavenly yeshiva wanted רבה to decide the case where we don't know which came first (step 13). He rules טהור, the same as הקב"ה. The בת קול plays on the word: his ruling was 'pure', his body was pure, and he died while saying 'pure'.

keyTerms.meaning: His soul is resting; a gentle way to say someone is dying

phrases.english: As his soul was coming to rest (as he was dying),
he said: Pure, pure.
A heavenly voice came out and said:
Fortunate are you, Rabba bar Nachmani,
for your body is pure,
and your soul left you with the word 'pure.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the story: after רבה says he would rather die, his death comes, and he rules on the heavenly question.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבה rules the unclear case טהור, and a בת קול praises his pure death.

steps.title: A note from heaven and the search for רבה's body
steps.stepSummary: A note falls in פומבדיתא announcing רבה's death; אביי, רבא and the חכמים search for him and find him where birds give shade.
steps.simpleTranslation: A note fell from the sky in פומבדיתא: 'רבה בר נחמני has been called to the heavenly yeshiva.' אביי, רבא and all the Rabbis went out to bury him, but they did not know where he was. They went to the swamp and saw birds making shade and staying in place. They said: 'This shows he is there.'
steps.whatsHappening: Heaven tells the חכמים that רבה has died, and they find his hidden body by a sign from the birds.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבה had been hiding in the swamp (step 11), so nobody knew where he was. The birds hovering to shade one spot show that even nature was honoring him, and that tells the חכמים where to find him.

keyTerms.meaning: Pumbedita, the city of רבה's yeshiva
To take care of him, meaning his burial

phrases.english: A note fell from the sky in Pumbedita:

phrases.aramaic: רַבָּה בַּר נַחְמָנִי נִתְבַּקֵּשׁ בִּיְשִׁיבָה שֶׁל מַעְלָה.
phrases.english: Rabba bar Nachmani has been summoned to the heavenly yeshiva.
Abaye and Rava and all the Rabbis went out
to take care of him (to bury him).
They did not know where he was.
They went to the swamp
and saw birds making shade and hovering in place.
They said: Learn from this, he is there.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the moment of death to how the חכמים on earth learned of it and found him.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Heaven announces רבה's death, and the birds lead the חכמים to his body.

steps.title: Heaven guides the mourning for רבה
steps.stepSummary: After three days of הספד, a note warns that anyone who leaves will be in נידוי; after seven days, a note sends them home in peace.
steps.simpleTranslation: They eulogized him for three days and three nights. A note fell: 'Anyone who leaves shall be in נידוי.' So they eulogized him for seven days. Another note fell: 'Go to your homes in peace.'
steps.whatsHappening: The חכמים mourn רבה, and heaven sends notes telling them to keep going and then telling them when to stop.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Three days was not enough honor for רבה, so heaven threatened נידוי on anyone who left early. Only after seven days did heaven release them. Heaven itself sets how much honor is due to him.

keyTerms.meaning: One who separates himself, here meaning one who leaves the mourning
A ban; being pushed away from the community

steps.whatToRemember: The story of רבה's death is full of heavenly signs: the בת קול, the notes, the birds, and the mourning set by heaven all show how great he was.

phrases.english: They eulogized him for three days and three nights.
A note fell:
Anyone who leaves shall be put in a ban.
phrases.notes: He means anyone who leaves the eulogy early.

phrases.english: They eulogized him for seven days.
A note fell: Go to your homes in peace.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After finding the body, the story moves on to the mourning.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Heaven required seven days of mourning for רבה and then sent the mourners home.

steps.title: A great storm on the day רבה died
steps.stepSummary: On the day רבה died, a storm carried an Arab merchant and his camel across a river; he prayed that the world not be destroyed over רבה, and the storm stopped.
steps.simpleTranslation: On the day he died, a storm lifted a certain Arab merchant while he was riding his camel, carried him from one side of נהר פפא, and threw him onto the other side. He asked: 'What is this?' They told him: 'רבה בר נחמני has died.' He said before God: 'Master of the World! The whole world is Yours, and רבה בר נחמני is Yours. You belong to רבה and רבה belongs to You. Why are You destroying the world?' The storm calmed.
steps.whatsHappening: The story shows that even the world of nature was shaken by רבה's death, until a stranger prayed and the storm stopped.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The merchant argues: רבה and the world both belong to הקב"ה, so why should the world suffer because רבה was taken? The prayer works and the storm stops. The point is how huge רבה's loss was felt to be.

phrases.english: On that day that he died,
a storm lifted and carried a certain Arab merchant
while he was riding a camel
from this side of the Pappa River
and threw him onto the other side.
He said: What is this?

phrases.aramaic: אָמְרִי לֵיהּ: נָח נַפְשֵׁיהּ דְּרַבָּה בַּר נַחְמָנִי.
phrases.english: They told him: Rabba bar Nachmani has died.
He said before God: Master of the World!
The whole world is Yours,
and Rabba bar Nachmani is Yours.
You are Rabba's, and Rabba is Yours.
Why are You destroying the world?
The storm calmed.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds one last sign of רבה's greatness on the day of his death, closing his story.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The world itself shook at רבה's death until a prayer calmed the storm.
steps.whatToRemember: This closes the story of רבה בר נחמני: his death was marked in heaven, among the חכמים, and even in nature.

steps.title: רבי שמעון בן חלפתא and the cooling wind
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא goes back to its stories of heavy חכמים: רבי שמעון בן חלפתא, feeling hot, promised his daughter spices for fanning him, and when a wind came he wondered how much he owed the Master of the wind.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי שמעון בן חלפתא was a heavy man. One day he was hot, so he went up and sat on a mountain rock. He said to his daughter: 'My daughter, fan me with a fan, and I will give you bundles of spikenard.' Meanwhile a wind blew. He said: 'How many bundles of spikenard do I owe the Master of this wind!'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts a new short story, going back to its earlier topic of heavy חכמים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: He was ready to pay his daughter well for a little fanning. When a strong natural wind came instead, he realized how much more he owes the One who sent it. A small comfort turns into a lesson in gratitude.

keyTerms.meaning: A rock or ledge of a mountain

steps.confusionAlert: This is not part of the רבה בר נחמני story. The גמרא has switched back to an earlier list of stories about heavy חכמים.

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן חֲלַפְתָּא בַּעַל בָּשָׂר הֲוָה.
phrases.english: Rabbi Shimon ben Chalafta was a heavy man.
One day he was hot,
so he went up and sat on a mountain rock.
He said to his daughter:
My daughter, fan me with a fan,
and I will give you bundles of spikenard.
Meanwhile, a wind blew.

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר: כַּמָּה כַּכְּרִין דְּנֵרְדְּ לְמָרֵי דֵּיכִי.
phrases.english: He said: How many bundles of spikenard do I owe the Master of this wind!

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן חֲלַפְתָּא בַּעַל בָּשָׂר הֲוָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the רבה story and returns to the earlier topic of heavy חכמים.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A natural wind is a gift worth far more than any payment for a fan, so one owes great thanks to its Master.

steps.title: What does the word 'everything' add?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא returns to the משנה's rule that everything follows local custom and asks what the word הכל comes to include.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה said: 'Everything follows the custom of the region,' and so on. The גמרא asks: What does the word 'everything' come to include?
steps.whatsHappening: The stories are over, and the גמרא goes back to the משנה about feeding workers. It quotes the rule 'everything follows local custom' and asks what the extra word 'everything' adds. This sets up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה could have said only 'follow local custom.' The word הכל seems extra, so the גמרא assumes it is there to teach a case we would not have known otherwise.

keyTerms.meaning: Everything; an inclusive word that the גמרא treats as adding a case
The custom of the region or place
What does it come to include?

phrases.english: Everything is according to the custom of the region, etc.
'Everything' comes to include what?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the aggadic material (steps 1-20: the end of the book of אדם הראשון, the רבה בר נחמני story, and the רבי שמעון בן חלפתא story) and returns to analyzing the משנה.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What additional case is included by the inclusive word הכל in the משנה.

steps.title: Workers can refuse to change the local eating custom
steps.stepSummary: הכל includes a place where workers customarily eat bread and drink wine. The employer cannot make them come early and eat on the job.
steps.simpleTranslation: It comes to include a place where people usually eat bread and drink a quarter-לוג of wine. If the employer told them, 'Come early, and I will bring you the food,' they can say to him, 'That is not up to you.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question: 'everything' teaches that even the details of how and when workers eat follow local custom. The employer cannot change the custom on his own.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The new point is that local custom protects the workers even against small changes. An employer who wants to save work time by having them come early and eat in the field cannot force this. The workers can answer, 'לא כל כמינך,' meaning it is not in your power.

keyTerms.meaning: It is not in your power

phrases.english: To include a place where they are accustomed
to eat bread and drink a quarter-log of wine.
For if he (the employer) said to them,
'Come early, and I will bring it to you,'
phrases.notes: He wants them to start work early and get their food at work, so no work time is lost.

phrases.english: they can say to him: 'It is not in your power.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 21.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: הכל includes a place where workers customarily eat bread and drink wine: the employer cannot force them to come early and receive their food at work.
steps.whyThisMatters: It shows that local custom fully binds the employer, even on small details of the workers' meals.

steps.title: The story seems to contradict the rule
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה's story of רבן יוחנן בן מתיא and asks how a story can be brought that seems to go against the rule just taught.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה tells a story about רבן יוחנן בן מתיא, who said to his son, 'Go out and hire workers,' and so on. The גמרא asks: A story that contradicts the rule?!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes the story in the משנה, where the son promised the workers food and the father said that such an open promise could not be met even with a feast like שלמה's. It asks why the משנה brings a story that seems to go against its own rule of following local custom.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A story in a משנה is usually brought to support the rule just stated. Here the story shows that once food was promised, local custom no longer sets the limit, so it looks like it goes against the rule of 'everything follows local custom' instead of supporting it.

keyTerms.meaning: A story or incident brought as an example
The חכם in the משנה's story who sent his son to hire workers

phrases.english: There was an incident with רבן יוחנן בן מתיא
who said to his son, 'Go out and hire,' etc.
An incident to contradict?!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves to the next part of the משנה and points out a problem with how it is built.
steps.kashyaTarget: The way the משנה is organized: the rule of local custom followed by the story of רבן יוחנן בן מתיא.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A story should support the rule before it, but this story seems to go against the rule of following local custom.

steps.title: The משנה is missing words: 'But if he promised them food'
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that the משנה is missing some words. It should read: everything follows custom, but if the employer promised food, a new rule applies.
steps.simpleTranslation: Words are missing from the משנה, and this is what it is teaching: 'But if he promised them food...'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא solves the problem by saying the משנה left out a line. It starts to fill in the missing words: the case where the employer made a promise about food.
steps.deeperAnalysis: With the added line, the story no longer goes against the rule. It illustrates a separate case: a promise of food, which is different from plain local custom. The full wording continues past this point.

keyTerms.meaning: Words are missing from the text
And this is what it is teaching

steps.confusionAlert: 'Words are missing' does not mean the משנה has a mistake. It is a common way the גמרא shows that the משנה speaks briefly, and the גמרא spells out the full meaning.

phrases.english: It is missing words, and this is what it teaches:
'And if he promised them food,'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of step 23.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Filling in missing words in the משנה (חסורי מחסרא)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The story was illustrating the rule of local custom, so it seemed to contradict that rule.
steps.terutzMaskana: The story illustrates a separate added case, where the employer promised food, so it does not contradict the rule of local custom.
